summary: Construct the quotient-deformation comparison for generic noncritical crystabelline (φ,Γ)-modules and use its kernel to select a minimal locally analytic representation of GL_n(K). The plan proves parabolic and embedding compatibility, recovery of modified Hodge flags, scalar character statements, and the first-order Artinian universal-extension reformulation. Its two input theories are imported with explicit supplier contracts; the parts of them already planned elsewhere (distribution algebras, Robba and rank-one modules, labelled de Rham realizations, the modified object D_σ, the (φ,Γ)-module deformation rings and the principal-series Bernstein centre) are consumed from their owners. This completes the design pass, conditional on the three explicitly recorded supplier gaps; it is not a closed or implemented theory.

inputContracts.statement: The category of admissible locally Q_p-analytic E-representations of GL_n(K), strong continuous duality with coadmissible distribution modules, and Ext¹ as Yoneda extensions; its identification with Ext in the category of abstract distribution modules with arguments reversed. Supply push-forward, pullback, exact Hom–Ext sequences, finite coefficient tensor products, tautological extension classes and subspace detection under scalar endomorphisms. The distribution algebras D(H,E) of compact open H⊂GL_n(K), their Fréchet–Stein structure and the abelian category of coadmissible modules are LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.1/distribution-algebra and ND.2/coadmissible-theorems, consumed from there; this contract is the passage to GL_n(K), admissibility and the Ext calculus.

Supply π_sm(φ), L(λ), A, PS(w(φ),h), PS_1, C(I,s_{i,σ}), V=π_1(φ,h), π(φ,h), the specified embeddings and first two socle layers. Supply End(π)→End(V)→End(A)≃E, Ext¹(A,V)≃Ext¹(A,π), and Lemma 3.5(2) with constituent dévissage used for push-forward surjectivity. Labels use all nonempty proper I⊂{1,…,n}, not I⊂{1,…,n−1}.

Supply injective ζ_w:H_T→B with images B_w; dim B=n+(2^n−1)d_K, dim B_w=n(1+d_K), and Σ_wB_w=B. Supply common B_g and B_g′, B_g≤B_g′≤B_w, with dim B_g=n and dim B_g′=n+d_K. Supply smooth parameter compatibility and Weyl invariance on actual block determinant directions.

Supply normalized parabolic Ext images B_F, the isomorphism ζ_F:∏B(M_i)≃B_F, compatible-refinement spanning, and 0→B_g′→B_F⊕B_G→B→0 for the two endpoint parabolics, with first arrow b↦(b,−b). Supply π_F and its inclusion, Emerton induction I_{P⁻}^G, completed external tensor product, and their extension-class compatibilities. Use θ_P constant −Σ_{k<i}n_k on block i and twist ε⁻¹∘θ_P.

Supply π_{1,σ}, Ext¹_σ(A,π_{1,σ}) and its image B_σ⊂B, with algebraicity at every τ≠σ, dim B_σ=n+2^n−1. Supply the partially algebraic Hom–Ext and parabolic compatibilities, the common smooth space, and ⊕_σ(B_σ/B_g)≃B/B_g. Supply the analogous amalgamation of π_{1,σ} over A and its maximal partial algebraic subrepresentations.

Supply the Jacquet–Emerton/Orlik–Strauch character-to-Ext compatibility (3.10), Proposition 3.6(1), Remark 3.7 and the surjectivity in (3.14), including their use on the universal character extension. The completed principal-series Bernstein centre Ĥ_φ, the maps 𝒥_w and their smooth tangent compatibility are already planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3 (part-ii-principal-series-centre, part-ii-ordered-character-map, part-ii-principal-series-completion, part-ii-principal-series-tangent) and are consumed from there.

The theory includes nonétale objects. The Robba ring, rank-one modules R_{K,E}(δ) with the criterion that R_{K,E}(δ) is de Rham exactly when δ is locally algebraic, Ext¹ as first-order deformations, labelled de Rham realizations and B-pairs are already planned (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.1/rank-one-dictionary, PG.3/herr-ext, PG.7/rank-one-characters; PadicHodgeTheory P7/labelled-bdr-realisation, P7/b-pair-robba-equivalence) and are consumed from there.

nodes.title: Endpoint refinement families
nodes.statement: For n≥1, define S_end={w∈S_n | w(n)=n} and S_start={w∈S_n | w(n)=1}. The paper uses w(φ)_i=φ_{w⁻¹(i)}, so these are exactly the refinements placing φ_n last or first. S_end is the standard subgroup S_{n−1}; S_start is a coset, and each has (n−1)! elements. Suggested Lean uses Fin(m+1), with m=n−1.
hypotheses: n≥1; permutations act by w(φ)_i=φ_{w⁻¹(i)}.
proofSteps: Identify S_end with permutations of the complement of n.
Choose a permutation moving n to 1 and translate S_end to S_start; verify the permutation convention before using these families in induction.
acceptance: Check both cardinalities and their membership tests.
Do not substitute w⁻¹(n)=1 for w(n)=1.

nodes.title: Block character subspaces
nodes.statement: Identify H_T with H_char^n, H_char=Hom_la(K×,E), by ψ(t)=Σ_i ψ_i(t_i). For 1≤j<n put H_j={ (a,…,a,b,…,b) : a,b∈H_char }, with j entries a, and H_Z={ (a,…,a) }. These are images of pullback along the two block determinants and the full determinant. They realize the character spaces of the Levi centers inside H_T; they are not obtained by reversing restriction along Z_j⊂T. For 0≤j≤n define blockTuple(n,j,a,b)_i=a for i<j and b otherwise (zero-based).
hypotheses: K,E as in H; n≥1. For the tuple model alone, an additive commutative group suffices.
proofSteps: Use the product decomposition T(K)=(K×)^n to identify additive characters with tuples.
Pull a character of K××K× back by (∏_{i≤j}t_i,∏_{i>j}t_i); differentiate if a center restriction is used.
Restriction to scalar blocks multiplies the corresponding characters by j and n−j, invertible over E.
acceptance: Keep H_Z⊂H_j explicit.
Use locally Q_p-analytic additive characters; dimensions are 1+d_K per coordinate.

nodes.title: Levi-center character spanning
nodes.statement: H_T=H_Z+Σ_{j=1}^{n−1}H_j. More precisely, for v=(v_0,…,v_{n−1}) in H_char^n, v is the constant tuple v_{n−1} plus Σ_{j=1}^{n−1}blockTuple(n,j,v_{j−1}−v_j,0). This also holds over any additive commutative group. The sum is a spanning sum with overlaps, not a direct-sum isomorphism as printed in (3.43).
hypotheses: n≥1; H_char an additive commutative group, specialized to Hom_la(K×,E).
proofSteps: At coordinate i the terms with j>i telescope to v_i−v_{n−1}.
Each summand is a two-block character; for n=1 only the constant summand remains.
For an interior position i and split j, the block containing i reaches either 1 or n, so its Weyl group contains a permutation sending i to an endpoint.
acceptance: Check the coordinate formula rather than a dimension-only argument.

Via ζ_F,κ_F and ζ_G,κ_G define t_F:B_F→Q_F↪Q and t_G:B_G→Q_G↪Q by the smaller-rank comparisons and the rank-one character map. These maps agree on B_g′. Hence there is a unique τ_D:B→Q restricting to both, by 0→B_g′→B_F⊕B_G→B→0 with anti-diagonal first arrow. It satisfies the refinement equation for w(n)=n or w(n)=1.
hypotheses: Standing hypotheses H: n≥1; K/Q_p finite; E/Q_p finite containing every embedding of K; φ=(φ_i) smooth with φ_i/φ_j∉{1,|·|_K} for i≠j; h_{i,σ}>h_{i+1,σ}; D∈ΦΓ_nc(φ,h), with every refinement noncritical. Input contracts LA and TR in the reader, and gaps G-LA/G-TR, apply whenever their objects are used.

sourceIssues.locator: DING25, published version: proof of Proposition 3.26, the bijection HC:X_h→X_{ξ_λ}, p. 51
sourceIssues.printed: The map between the tangent spaces of U(t_{Σ_K}) at h and of its Weyl invariants at the image point is said to be bijective because the invariants form a polynomial algebra.
sourceIssues.correction: The tangent map of Spec U(t_{Σ_K})→Spec U(t_{Σ_K})^{W} is bijective at h because h is regular: at each σ the Jacobian of the elementary symmetric polynomials at (h_{1,σ},…,h_{n,σ}) is, up to sign, the Vandermonde determinant ∏_{i<j}(h_{i,σ}−h_{j,σ}), which is nonzero since h is strictly dominant.
sourceIssues.reason: Polynomiality of the invariants alone does not give the bijection: for n=2 at a point with equal coordinates the Jacobian of (x_1+x_2,x_1x_2) is singular, so the tangent map is not injective there.
